scenes.prompt_gemini:
STYLE ANCHOR: public/assets/sonjata-papercraft/clips/scene5a-kenburns-source.png — match this exact paper-craft style.

Paper-craft illustration, 9:16 vertical. SCENE: The same Mali throne room as before — now with a different man claiming the throne. Mansa Moussa, the richest human being in all of history, ascends to power.

MANSA MOUSSA ON THE THRONE:
Mansa Moussa seated on the carved ebony throne, in a position of absolute authority. He is visibly more LAVISHLY adorned than Abou Bakari:
- Dark brown skin, broader build, strong features, dot-eyes
- Grand boubou in deep gold-yellow with crimson embroidery and geometric patterns — overwhelming richness
- Elaborate gold diadem (more ornate than Abou Bakari's), gold armbands stacked high, multiple cowrie and gold bead necklaces
- Seated fully upright, commanding posture, both hands on armrests
- He is NOT lost in thought — he OWNS the room, gaze forward and assured
- The same throne room, same guards, but feel is of arrival and consolidation
- SAME architecture as Empire scene: ochre adobe walls, incised geometric patterns, warm gold beams through arched doorways

STYLE for both: Sonjata paper-craft — thick black outlines, flat color fills. WARM GOLD palette dominant — this is the richest single image in the film.

CRITICAL TECHNICAL RULES:
- Strict dot-eyes on Mansa Moussa
- No text, no writing, no readable inscriptions
- Mali XIVe century: NO European elements
- 9:16 vertical (1080x1920)
scenes.prompt_seedance:

Camera executes a slow cinematic arc — starting frontal, curving 30 degrees to the RIGHT to reveal the throne's carved wood details and the tapestries behind. Smooth wide curve.

SECONDS 0 TO 3: The king on the throne in WHITE-AND-GOLD robes SITS with composed authority. His posture is UPRIGHT, head LIFTED. He holds a golden scepter in his RIGHT hand — fingers CLOSED firmly around it, scepter RIGID and NON-DEFORMING, length CONSTANT throughout. The gold necklace at his chest CATCHES ambient light. SKIN: the king has DARK BROWN skin — clearly visible.

SECONDS 3 TO 6: The two courtiers standing to the LEFT SHIFT — the one in the front BOWS more deeply, the one behind CLASPS hands. The child figure on the RIGHT side STANDS straight, attentive. The two wall torches FLICKER — left torch flame BENDS right, right torch flame BENDS left, both alive with movement. The geometric indigo tapestries on the back wall BREATHE minimally.

SECONDS 6 TO 10: The king TURNS his gaze slowly toward the camera — a deliberate, regal look. His expression is measured, powerful. The scepter REMAINS in his RIGHT hand, RIGID and UNMOVING in his grip. The courtiers maintain their poses, micro-shifting. The torches continue FLICKERING.

COLOR GRADE: warm amber adobe walls, deep indigo and gold tapestries, white-gold royal robes, warm torchlight glow — paper-craft palette throughout. All characters stay engaged. No dust motes, no floating particles, no sparkles. No text anywhere.

scenes.prompt_gemini:
STYLE ANCHOR: public/assets/sonjata-papercraft/clips/scene5a-kenburns-source.png — match this exact paper-craft style.

Paper-craft illustration, 9:16 vertical. SCENE: The open Atlantic, 1311. A single royal pirogue seen from above and behind, moving westward into the fog. The figure of Abou Bakari visible at the prow — small against the vast ocean, his back to us.

COMPOSITION:
- The pirogue occupies the lower-center of the frame, moving away from us toward the horizon
- Abou Bakari at the prow: back to us, standing, arms slightly outstretched toward the western horizon — a figure of pure obsession
- The western horizon ahead: the fog wall from Scene 1 is there, but now there is a faint warm golden light behind it — something unknown
- The ocean around the pirogue: deep Atlantic blue-black, churning swells, white foam at the prow
- Sky: transitioning from warm ochre behind (east, the known world) to deep indigo ahead (west, the unknown)

PALETTE: the scene is split — warm ochre-gold light behind the pirogue (all that was left behind), deep cold indigo ahead (the unknown). The pirogue is the bridge between worlds.

CRITICAL TECHNICAL RULES:
- No text, no writing
- Abou Bakari back-to-camera — maintains mystery
- 9:16 vertical (1080x1920)

scenes.prompt_gemini:
STYLE ANCHOR: public/assets/sonjata-papercraft/clips/scene5a-kenburns-source.png — match this exact paper-craft style.

Paper-craft illustration, 9:16 vertical. SCENE: The Atlantic Ocean, 1492 — 181 years after Abou Bakari. A European caravel under full sail, the Santa Maria or similar vessel, crossing the same Atlantic.

COMPOSITION: The caravel dominates the upper-center frame, under full sail. Three white square sails, large red cross of the Order of Christ painted on the main sail. High wooden prow and stern castle. European crewmen visible on deck as small paper-craft silhouettes.

KEY CONTRAST ELEMENTS (this is the CONTRAST scene):
- The ocean is the SAME Atlantic — same deep blue water as Abou Bakari's scenes
- But the sky is COLDER — no warm ochre, pale grey-blue European sky
- The ship is massive, complex, loud compared to the pirogue
- A small inset silhouette in one corner (bottom-left): the ghost outline of a Mali pirogue — the memory of what came before

STYLE: Sonjata paper-craft — thick black outlines, flat color fills. PALETTE SHIFT: cold European grey-blue palette for the sky, the sails white-grey, the ship dark wood — deliberately contrasting with the warm sepia-gold of all previous scenes.

CRITICAL TECHNICAL RULES:
- Strict dot-eyes on any crew figures visible
- No text, no readable writing
- COLD palette (deliberate break from warm sepia)
- 9:16 vertical (1080x1920)

COLOR GRADE: cold blue-grey ocean, white sails, dark grey hull, pale cool sky — deliberately COLD and MONOCHROMATIC, zero warm tones, no amber, no sepia — intentional contrast with the African palette. No dust motes, no floating particles, no sparkles. No text anywhere.
